lessons.title: Opening takbir
lessons.question: What does this phrase proclaim?
lessons.note: Raising the hands and saying Allahu Akbar marks the transition from ordinary concerns into prayer. Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari 757 and Sahih Muslim 601.

lessons.title: Al-Fatiha · ayah 1
lessons.meaning: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
lessons.question: In whose name does the ayah begin?
lessons.note: Beginning with Bismillah places the entire recitation under Allah's name and mercy. Note: the audio player above recites the full Surah Al-Fatiha.

passage.translation: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.

lessons.title: Al-Fatiha · ayah 2
lessons.meaning: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds,
lessons.question: Who receives praise in this ayah?
lessons.note: Al-hamdu lillah combines gratitude with praise—recognizing Allah as Rabb, the Sustainer and Caretaker of all creation.

passage.translation: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds,

lessons.title: Al-Fatiha · ayah 3
lessons.question: Which descriptions appear in this ayah?
lessons.note: Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim both come from the root for mercy (rahmah), echoing the opening ayah and framing Allah's lordship in compassion.

lessons.title: Al-Fatiha · ayah 4
lessons.meaning: Master of the Day of Judgment,
lessons.question: Which day is named?
options: The Day of Gathering on Friday
lessons.note: Yawm ad-Din is the Day of Recompense, when every deed is weighed with complete justice and no authority remains except Allah's.

passage.translation: Master of the Day of Judgment,

lessons.title: Al-Fatiha · ayah 5
lessons.meaning: Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help.
lessons.question: To whom are worship and the request for help directed?
lessons.note: Putting 'Thee alone' (Iyyaka) first in Arabic makes both worship and seeking help exclusive to Allah—a turning point where the surah shifts into direct address.

passage.translation: Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help.

lessons.title: Al-Fatiha · ayah 6
lessons.question: What is requested?
lessons.note: After praise and devotion comes the core request of every rak'ah: steady guidance on the clear, upright path (as-sirat al-mustaqim).

lessons.title: Al-Fatiha · ayah 7
lessons.arabic: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
lessons.meaning: The path of those whom Thou hast favoured; Not the (path) of those who earn Thine anger nor of those who go astray.
lessons.question: Whose path is requested?
options: Those who rely on their own strength
lessons.note: The closing ayah defines the straight path by the people who walked it—those blessed with guidance—while asking to be kept from both willful rejection and heedless wandering.

passage.arabic: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
passage.translation: The path of those whom Thou hast favoured; Not the (path) of those who earn Thine anger nor of those who go astray.

lessons.title: Bowing · glorification
lessons.meaning: Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent.
lessons.question: How is the Lord described in this phrase?
lessons.note: In ruku', bowing your back physically mirrors the words: declaring Allah free of all imperfection and affirming His greatness (Al-Azim).

lessons.title: Rising from bowing
lessons.meaning: Allah hears the one who praises Him.
lessons.question: Whose praise is mentioned?
options: The one who fasts in secret
lessons.note: Said while rising from bowing, 'Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah' is both a statement and an assurance: Allah hears and responds to anyone who praises Him.

lessons.title: Praise while standing
lessons.meaning: Our Lord, praise belongs to You.
lessons.question: What is directed to the Lord?
lessons.note: Once standing upright again, you answer the previous phrase directly—offering praise to your Lord before moving into prostration.

lessons.title: Prostration · glorification
lessons.meaning: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.
lessons.question: Which description appears here?
lessons.note: At the lowest physical point of prayer, with forehead on the ground, you call upon Allah as Al-A'la—the Most High.

lessons.title: Tashahhud · testimony
lessons.arabic: التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ، وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
lessons.meaning: Greetings, prayers, and good things belong to Allah. Peace, Allah’s mercy, and His blessings be upon you, Prophet. Peace be upon us and Allah’s righteous servants. I testify that none is worthy of worship except Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.
lessons.question: How is Muhammad ﷺ described at the end of this wording?
lessons.note: Follows the tashahhud narrated by Ibn Mas'ud in Sahih al-Bukhari. Calling Muhammad ﷺ both servant ('abd) and messenger (rasul) honors his mission while keeping worship for Allah alone. Other authentic wordings exist, such as Sahih Muslim 403a.

lessons.title: Sending blessings
lessons.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
lessons.meaning: O Allah, bestow prayers upon Muhammad and his family as You bestowed prayers upon Ibrahim and his family. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and his family as You blessed Ibrahim and his family. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
lessons.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad…
lessons.question: Which earlier prophet is named?
lessons.note: Known as as-salat al-Ibrahimiyyah, this supplication asks Allah to bless Muhammad ﷺ and his family just as He blessed Ibrahim and his family. Other authentic wordings are also narrated.

lessons.title: The closing greeting
lessons.meaning: Peace and Allah’s mercy be upon you.

sources.label: Sahih Muslim 431 · Arabic institutional edition
sources.note: Arabic text hosted by the Saudi General Presidency of Scholarly Research and Ifta.

lessons.question: What does this greeting wish for its recipients?
lessons.note: Turning right and left with salam closes the prayer by extending peace and Allah's mercy to the angels and everyone praying beside you.

methodology: Fifteen lessons walk through Surah Al-Fatiha and the core recitations of prayer from opening takbir to closing salam. Quranic passages use Uthmani Arabic with Pickthall's translation; hadith recitations use concise English renderings alongside cited reports. Use this as a guide to the meanings of prayer rather than a complete fiqh manual. The built-in audio recording plays the full Surah Al-Fatiha.
